body: TASER International renamed itself Axon in April 2017 (after its body-camera and Evidence.com cloud unit) and offered every US police department free body cameras and a year of cloud storage — converting one-time hardware sales into multi-year subscription bundles (cameras + TASER + cloud + later Fusus, drones, AI report-writing 'Draft One'). Founder-CEO Rick Smith got a 2018 market-cap-milestone award. Stock ~$24 (2017 rebrand) [unverified] -> 52-week highs ~$800-880 in 2025 [unverified] ≈ 35x; +600% since 2020 per 2025 coverage. ARR $1.2bn (Q2 2025) from $850m a year earlier; Q4 2025 revenue +39% to $797m; stock +16-17% on Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 prints. Only ~30% of customers on premium plans (Q4 2025) = upsell runway. Split: largely rerating (EV/sales from ~4x to ~20x+) on a recurring-revenue mix shift, plus revenue ~6x [approx]. Drawdown: ~-50% in 2021-22 [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2017-19: the free-camera land-grab, rising Evidence.com seats and multi-year bookings (RPO) disclosed each quarter, gross margin rising as software mix grew. Who caught it: growth funds; no single documented name found. LESSON: a hardware incumbent that gives away the device to lock in software subscriptions in a sticky government market can rerate from hardware to SaaS multiples; watch ARR and RPO, not unit sales.

data.early_signals: free body-camera offer; Evidence.com seats; RPO growth; GM rising
data.lesson: razor/blade to SaaS in sticky gov market; track ARR/RPO

title: Axon (ex-TASER) 2017-2025: hardware to public-safety SaaS, ~35x
